script: Giant rogue waves were once thought to be sailors' myths. That changed on January 1, 1995, at the Draupner oil platform in the North Sea. Instruments there measured a single wave about 26 meters high. It was more than twice as tall as the waves around it. Rogue waves can appear suddenly, even in fairly ordinary storms. Satellites have since shown they happen more often than anyone expected. Follow Pixel Abyss for more strange facts from the deep.
